description:
Definition diagram: a plan of a left jogged intersection. The arterial street runs horizontally across the sheet with two curb lines. The minor street meets it in two offset legs, one entering from the top left and one from the bottom right. A car on the top-left leg is shown with two dashed sight lines marking angle theta 2, the angle between the motorist looking straight ahead and the back of the opposing vehicle on the other leg. A car on the bottom-right leg is shown the same way with a dashed vertical centerline and angle theta 1. A box in the middle of the arterial marks the intersection area. Two small vertical ticks across the arterial mark the real or hypothetical interior limit lines, and the dimension D is drawn between them (it appears once near the lower-left signal pole and once near the upper-right pole where the dashed sight lines cross). Two mastarm signal poles are drawn, one on the lower side of the arterial near the left end and one on the upper side near the right end, each with a head and an arrow. Dimension X2 runs along the arterial on the lower-left from the crosswalk line at the left to the lower signal pole. Dimension X1 runs along the arterial at the upper right from the upper signal pole to the crosswalk line at the right.

Definitions block: text above the plan defines theta 1 and theta 2, X1 and X2, and D.

Selection procedure: four numbered steps below the plan (jog direction, D, theta 1 and theta 2, then X1 and X2) with the thresholds 40 ft for D, 20 degrees for theta and 50 ft for X, and cross-references to Sheets 3 through 12. The sheet number in the title block is 2 of 12 and the drawing number is S-100.0 for the City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation.
notes:
Definitions:
theta 1 and theta 2 = angle between a motorist looking straight ahead and the back of the opposing vehicle.
X1 and X2 = distance along the arterial from the crosswalk line or limit line to the signal pole or BCR at the far side of the first intersecting leg.
D = internal storage distance between real or hypothetical interior limit lines. For a minor offset D may be a small or negative number.

To select the most appropriate design:
1. Determine if there is a left jog or a right jog. See Sheets 3, 5, 7, 9, 10 and 11 for left jogged intersections and Sheets 4, 6, 8 and 12 for right jogged intersections.
2. Determine D. If D >= 40' then interior limit lines are required. If D < 40' then the jog is operated as a single intersection. See Sheets 10, 11 and 12 for intersections with interior limit lines and Sheets 3 through 9 for single intersection operation.
3. Determine theta 1 and theta 2. If theta 1 or theta 2 is > 20 degrees and D < 40' then some form of opposed phasing is required for the minor street. See Sheets 7 through 9 for situations requiring opposed phasing. See Sheets 3 through 6 for situations for which concurrent phasing is adequate. Note that for Sheets 4 and 6 opposed phasing is required if diagonal crosswalks are not feasible, due to the unexpected presence of pedestrians crossing the path of right-turning motorists.
4. Determine X1 and X2. If X1 and X2 >= 50' and D < 40' then only internal mastarms are to be used on the arterial street. If X1 and X2 < 50' then only external mastarms are to be used on the arterial street. See Sheets 3, 4, 7 and 8 for internal mastarm designs and Sheets 5, 6 and 9 for external mastarm designs.

Note: The drawings on Sheets 3 through 12 are not intended to show the required safety lighting design. Final lighting designs may not include the depicted mastarm lighting and likely will include other lighting locations not shown.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections (Sheet 2 of 12)
summary: Sheet 2 of 12 of drawing S-100.0 gives the definitions of theta 1, theta 2, X1, X2 and D and a four-step procedure for choosing a jogged-intersection signal design. The steps test jog direction, internal storage distance D (40 ft), the sight angles (20 degrees) and the mastarm distances X1 and X2 (50 ft), and point to the plan sheets for each case.

description:
Plan view, Left jogged intersection, internal mastarms: the arterial runs vertically with a two-way left-turn lane marked by a double centerline and a left-turn arrow in the upper half and another in the lower half. The minor street crosses it in two offset legs, one entering at the lower left and one at the upper right, with a car shown on each leg and dashed sight lines marking theta 2 (left leg) and theta 1 (right leg). A dashed curve through the intersection is labeled R=30' min. Four internal mastarm poles stand inside the intersection: two on the left side (lower pole at the left corner of the lower-left leg and a pole just above it) and two on the right side, each with a signal head symbol and arrows for phases 2, 4, 6 and 8. Next to the two inner poles are R9-3a signs (shown as R9-3a'S) and a callout reading WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC. Pedestrian heads are labeled 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P at the corners, each with an APS pushbutton. Vehicle arrows near the corners carry phase labels 2, 4, 6 and 8. Dimension X2 is drawn on the left from the upper crosswalk line down to the R9-3a sign at the left inner pole. Dimension X1 is drawn on the right from the R9-3a sign at the right inner pole down to the lower crosswalk line.

Phase key: The phase key is a 2 by 4 grid of boxes numbered 1 to 8. Boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out (not used). Box 2 shows a solid down arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 4 shows a solid left arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow above it. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow.

Title block caption: Left jogged intersection, internal mastarms. Sheet 3 of 12, drawing S-100.0.
notes:
1. Install where:
a) D < 40', and
b) theta 1 and theta 2 <= 20 degrees, and
c) X1 and X2 >= 50'.
2. The beveled visors shown should be installed only where cross-traffic motorists would see 50% or more of the lens area of a far-side signal as they wait at the limit line. Programmed visibility (PV) heads should be used if beveled visors would not be adequate.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections: Left Jogged Intersection, Internal Mastarms (Sheet 3 of 12)
summary: Sheet 3 of 12 shows a left jogged intersection with internal mastarms and concurrent minor street phasing. It applies where D is under 40 ft, theta 1 and theta 2 are 20 degrees or less, and X1 and X2 are 50 ft or more. Beveled visors are allowed only where cross-traffic would see at least half of a far-side lens.

description:
Plan view, Right jogged intersection, prohibited left turn: the arterial runs vertically. The minor street meets it in two offset legs, the left leg at the upper left and the right leg at the lower right, with a car on each leg and dashed sight lines marking theta 1 and theta 2. Two long parallel diagonal lines run from the upper-left leg to the lower-right leg and mark the diagonal crosswalks across the arterial, with R3-2 signs at two places along them. A dashed curve is labeled RCR=30' MIN. A dimension of 15' MIN. is drawn at the lower part of the diagonal band beside a curved median nose. The upper part of the arterial has a left-turn arrow marking. The lower part shows channelization with a curved median nose where the left turn is prohibited in that direction. A thick bar with the label R/C stands at the left curb line near the lower-left corner. Signal poles carry heads and arrows for phases 2, 4, 6 and 8, with callouts WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC at three places. Pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P and APS pushbuttons sit at the corners. Dimension X2 is drawn on the left side of the upper-left leg and X1 on the right side of the lower-right leg.

Phase key: The phase key is a 2 by 4 grid of boxes numbered 1 to 8. Boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out (not used). Box 2 shows a solid down arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 4 shows a solid left arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow above it. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow.

Title block caption: Right jogged intersection, prohibited left turn. Sheet 4 of 12, drawing S-100.0.
notes:
1. Install where:
a) D < 40', and
b) theta 1 and theta 2 <= 20 degrees, and
c) X1 and X2 >= 50', and
d) diagonal crosswalks are feasible.
2. Where diagonal crosswalks are not feasible, use opposed phasing, as shown on Sheet 8.
3. The treatment to allow arterial left turns in one direction and prohibit them in the other direction is an operational option. For other typical left turn operations on the arterial street see Sheets 6 and 8.
4. The beveled visors shown should be installed only where cross-traffic motorists would see 50% or more of the lens area of a far-side signal as they wait at the limit line. Programmed visibility (PV) heads should be used if beveled visors would not be adequate.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections: Right Jogged Intersection, Prohibited Left Turn (Sheet 4 of 12)
summary: Sheet 4 of 12 shows a right jogged intersection with internal mastarms, diagonal crosswalks and a prohibited arterial left turn in one direction. It applies where D is under 40 ft, theta 1 and theta 2 are 20 degrees or less, X1 and X2 are 50 ft or more and diagonal crosswalks are feasible. Opposed phasing on Sheet 8 is the fallback where diagonal crosswalks are not feasible.

description:
Plan view, Left jogged intersection, external mastarms: the arterial runs vertically with a double centerline and left-turn arrows in the upper and lower portions. The minor street enters in two offset legs, the left leg lower and the right leg upper, with a car on each leg and dashed sight lines marking theta 1 and theta 2. A dashed curve is labeled R=30' min. Mastarm poles stand outside the intersection at the arterial corners (external). At the lower left a mastarm for phase 2 extends over the arterial, with phase 2 and phase 4 arrows at the curb. R9-3a signs (shown as R9-3a'S) with WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC callouts stand at the inner corners of the legs. Pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P with APS pushbuttons sit at the corners. Dimension X2 is drawn on the left from the upper crosswalk line down to the left R9-3a sign. Dimension X1 is drawn on the right from the right R9-3a sign down to the lower crosswalk line.

Phase key: The phase key is a 2 by 4 grid of boxes numbered 1 to 8. Boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out (not used). Box 2 shows a solid down arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 4 shows a solid left arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow above it. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow.

Title block caption: Left jogged intersection, external mastarms. Sheet 5 of 12, drawing S-100.0.
notes:
1. Install where:
a) D < 40', and
b) theta 1 and theta 2 <= 20 degrees, and
c) X1 and X2 < 50'.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections: Left Jogged Intersection, External Mastarms (Sheet 5 of 12)
summary: Sheet 5 of 12 shows a left jogged intersection with external mastarms and concurrent minor street phasing. It applies where D is under 40 ft, theta 1 and theta 2 are 20 degrees or less, and X1 and X2 are under 50 ft.

description:
Plan view, Right jogged intersection, protected left turn: the arterial runs vertically. The minor street enters in two offset legs, the left leg at the upper left and the right leg at the lower right, with a car on each leg and dashed sight lines marking theta 1 and theta 2. Two long parallel diagonal lines across the arterial mark the diagonal crosswalks. External mastarm poles stand at the arterial corners with heads for phases 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8. Phase 5 heads use triple-arrow indications and appear near the lower left corner and at the lower-right pole, on the protected left-turn side. A left-turn arrow marking is shown at the top center of the arterial and another in the lower left-turn lane. WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC callouts appear on the poles at the upper right and lower left. Pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P with APS pushbuttons sit at the corners. Dimension X2 is drawn on the left of the upper-left leg and X1 on the right of the lower-right leg.

Phase key: boxes 1, 3 and 7 are crossed out (not used). Box 2 shows a solid down arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 4 shows a solid left arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow above it. Box 5 shows a curved arrow that starts upward and turns right (the protected left turn). Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow.

Title block caption: Right jogged intersection, protected left turn. Sheet 6 of 12, drawing S-100.0.
notes:
1. Install where:
a) D < 40', and
b) theta 1 and theta 2 <= 20 degrees, and
c) X1 and X2 < 50', and
d) diagonal crosswalks are feasible.
2. Where diagonal crosswalks are not feasible, use opposed phasing, as shown on Sheet 8.
3. If arterial left turns are to be allowed in both directions, at least one direction shall have protected left turns, as shown. For other typical left turn options on the arterial street see Sheets 4 and 8.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections: Right Jogged Intersection, Protected Left Turn (Sheet 6 of 12)
summary: Sheet 6 of 12 shows a right jogged intersection with external mastarms, diagonal crosswalks and a protected arterial left turn using phase 5. It applies where D is under 40 ft, theta 1 and theta 2 are 20 degrees or less, X1 and X2 are under 50 ft and diagonal crosswalks are feasible. If left turns are allowed both ways, at least one direction must be protected.

description:
Plan view, Left jogged intersection, internal mastarms, opposed phasing: the arterial runs vertically with a double centerline and left-turn arrows near the top and bottom. The minor street enters in two offset legs, the left leg lower and the right leg upper, with a car on each leg and dashed sight lines marking theta 1 and theta 2. The words KEEP CLEAR are painted twice in the box between the two legs, set between the interior limit lines. Dimension D is drawn on the right between the two interior limit lines. Dimension X2 is drawn on the left at the top and X1 on the right at the bottom. Internal mastarm poles with R9-3a signs (shown as R9-3a'S) carry heads for phases 2, 3, 4 and 6. Pedestrian heads 2P, 3P, 4P and 6P and APS pushbuttons sit at the corners.

Phase keys: the sheet shows three 2 by 4 phase grids. The first (standard opposed phasing) has boxes 1, 5, 7 and 8 crossed out. Box 2 shows a solid down arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 3 shows a solid right arrow with a curved branch arrow turning up and right, and a dashed two-headed arrow below. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid left arrow with a curved branch arrow turning down and left. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it.
Alternate 1: boxes 1, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 2 as above. Box 3 shows a solid right arrow with a curved branch arrow turning up and right. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid left arrow. Box 6 as above. Box 8 shows a dashed two-headed arrow only.
Alternate 2: boxes 1, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 2 as above. Box 3 shows a solid left arrow with a curved branch arrow turning down and left. Box 4 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow. Box 6 as above. Box 8 shows a dashed two-headed arrow only.

Title block caption: Left jogged intersection, internal mastarms, opposed phasing. Sheet 7 of 12, drawing S-100.0.
notes:
1. Install where:
a) D < 40', and
b) theta 1 or theta 2 > 20 degrees.
2. The alternate signal phasing schemes shown below, with corresponding signal head modifications (not shown), should be used only where the intersection would be operating near capacity with the more conventional opposed phasing. Generally, the alternate phasing would be necessary where pedestrian calls occur on most cycles. Where used, the lighter volume side street approach should have the left arrow indications. If one or both of the crosswalks across the arterial street can be eliminated, then the intersection operation can have more efficient phasing than shown.
3. Where D >= 20', "KEEP CLEAR" pavement markings should be installed between the cross street legs, as shown.
Phase key labels: Alternate 1, Alternate 2.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections: Left Jogged Intersection, Internal Mastarms, Opposed Phasing (Sheet 7 of 12)
summary: Sheet 7 of 12 shows a left jogged intersection with internal mastarms and opposed minor street phasing, including two alternate phasing schemes. It applies where D is under 40 ft and theta 1 or theta 2 exceeds 20 degrees. KEEP CLEAR markings go between the cross street legs where D is 20 ft or more.

description:
Plan view, Right jogged intersection, internal mastarms, opposed phasing: the arterial runs vertically. The minor street enters in two offset legs, the left leg at the upper left and the right leg at the lower right, with a car on each leg and dashed sight lines marking theta 1 and theta 2. The arterial has cat-tracked side-by-side left-turn lanes with a curved painted median. A dimension of 18' min. is drawn across the left-turn channelization at the top and again at the bottom. Two dimensions of 9' min. are drawn between dashed lane lines inside the intersection. Internal mastarm poles with R9-3a signs (shown as R9-3a'S) carry heads for phases 2, 3, 4 and 6. Pedestrian heads 2P, 3P, 4P and 6P with APS pushbuttons sit at the corners. Dimension X2 is drawn on the left of the upper-left leg and X1 on the right of the lower-right leg.

Phase keys: three 2 by 4 grids. Standard opposed phasing has boxes 1, 5, 7 and 8 crossed out. Box 2 shows a solid down arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 3 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid right arrow with a curved branch arrow turning down and right. Box 4 shows a solid left arrow with a curved branch arrow turning up and left above a dashed two-headed arrow. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it.
Alternate 1: boxes 1, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 3 shows a solid right arrow with a curved branch arrow turning down and right. Box 4 shows a solid left arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow. Box 8 shows a dashed two-headed arrow only. Boxes 2 and 6 as above.
Alternate 2: boxes 1, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 3 shows a solid left arrow with a curved branch arrow turning up and left. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid right arrow. Box 8 shows a dashed two-headed arrow only. Boxes 2 and 6 as above.

Title block caption: Right Jogged Intersection, Internal Mastarms, Opposed Phasing. Sheet 8 of 12, drawing S-100.0.
notes:
1. Install where:
a) D < 40', and
b) theta 1 or theta 2 > 20 degrees, and
c) X1 and X2 >= 50'.
2. The arterial, cat-tracked side-by-side left-turn lanes, as shown, are possible only where the painted median channelization is at least 18' wide. For other typical left turn options on the arterial street see Sheets 4 and 6.
3. The alternate signal phasing schemes shown below with corresponding signal head modifications should be used only where the intersection would be operating near capacity with the more conventional opposed phasing. Generally, the alternate phasing would be necessary where pedestrian calls occur on most cycles. Where used, the lighter volume side street approach should have the right arrow indications. If one or both of the crosswalks across the arterial street can be eliminated, then the intersection operation can have more efficient phasing than shown.
4. Where D >= 20', "KEEP CLEAR" pavement markings should be installed between the cross street legs, as shown in Sheet 7.
Phase key labels: Alternate 1, Alternate 2.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections: Right Jogged Intersection, Internal Mastarms, Opposed Phasing (Sheet 8 of 12)
summary: Sheet 8 of 12 shows a right jogged intersection with internal mastarms and opposed minor street phasing, with two alternate phasing schemes. It applies where D is under 40 ft, theta 1 or theta 2 exceeds 20 degrees and X1 and X2 are 50 ft or more. Cat-tracked side-by-side arterial left-turn lanes need a painted median at least 18 ft wide.

description:
Plan view, Left jogged intersection, external mastarms, opposed phasing: the arterial runs vertically with a double centerline and left-turn arrows near the top and bottom. The minor street enters in two offset legs, the left leg lower and the right leg upper, with a car on each leg and dashed sight lines marking theta 1 and theta 2 and a dashed curve labeled R=30' min. External mastarm poles stand at the arterial corners with heads and arrows for phases 2, 3, 4 and 6. R9-3a signs (shown as R9-3a'S) with a WATCH OPPOSING TRAFFIC callout stand at the inner corners. Pedestrian heads 2P, 3P, 4P and 6P with APS pushbuttons sit at the corners. Dimension X2 is drawn on the left at the top and X1 on the right at the bottom.

Phase key: one 2 by 4 grid with boxes 1, 5, 7 and 8 crossed out. Box 2 shows a solid down arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 3 shows a solid right arrow with a curved branch arrow turning up and right, with a dashed two-headed arrow below. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid left arrow with a curved branch arrow turning down and left. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it.

Title block caption: Left jogged intersection, external mastarms, opposed phasing. Sheet 9 of 12, drawing S-100.0.
notes:
1. Install where:
a) D < 40', and
b) theta 1 or theta 2 > 20 degrees, and
c) X1 and X2 < 50'.
2. See Sheet 7 for alternate signal phasing schemes.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections: Left Jogged Intersection, External Mastarms, Opposed Phasing (Sheet 9 of 12)
summary: Sheet 9 of 12 shows a left jogged intersection with external mastarms and opposed minor street phasing. It applies where D is under 40 ft, theta 1 or theta 2 exceeds 20 degrees and X1 and X2 are under 50 ft. Alternate phasing schemes are on Sheet 7.

description:
Plan view, Left jogged intersection, interior limit lines: the arterial runs vertically with a double centerline and left-turn arrows near the top and bottom. The minor street enters in two offset legs, the left leg lower and the right leg upper, separated along the arterial by a gap. Interior limit lines cross the arterial at both legs (one at the top of the intersection box and one at the bottom), and the lane lines between them are dashed. Dimension D is drawn on the left between the two interior limit lines. A curved median nose (double line) with a left-turn pocket sits inside the gap. Signal poles at the corners carry heads for phases 2, 4, 6 and 8, with R9-3a signs (shown as R9-3a'S) at the inner corners and mastarms over the arterial at both limit lines. Pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P with APS pushbuttons sit at the corners.

Phase key: a 2 by 4 grid. Boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 2 shows a solid down arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid left arrow. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow.

Title block caption: Left jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines. Sheet 10 of 12, drawing S-100.0.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections: Left Jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines (Sheet 10 of 12)
summary: Sheet 10 of 12 shows a left jogged intersection with interior limit lines, used where D is 40 ft or more. The two offset legs are signalized as separate intersections along the arterial, each with its own limit line and signal heads.

description:
Plan view, Left jogged intersection, interior limit lines, slot clearance: the arterial runs vertically with a double centerline and left-turn arrows near the top and bottom. The minor street enters in two offset legs, the left leg lower and the right leg upper, with interior limit lines drawn as rows of small circles across the arterial at the top and the bottom of the intersection box. Each row is labeled PV (G,R only), with callouts OLA PV CUT-OFF at the top and OLB PV CUT-OFF at the bottom. Overlap labels OLA and OLB appear on arrows and heads at the corners and along the limit lines. Dimension D is drawn on the left between the interior limit lines. A curved median nose sits in the gap. Mastarm poles carry heads and arrows for phases 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8, with phases 1 and 5 shown using triple-arrow indications. R9-3a signs (shown as R9-3a'S) stand at the inner corners. Pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P with APS pushbuttons sit at the corners.

Phase key: a 2 by 4 grid. Boxes 3 and 7 are crossed out. Box 1 is split by a dashed horizontal line: its lower half shows a curved left-turn arrow. Box 2 is split by a dashed line: the upper half shows a solid down arrow, and the lower half (labeled OLA) shows a dashed two-headed arrow beside a solid down arrow. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid left arrow. Box 5 is split: its upper half shows a curved arrow turning right, and the lower half is empty. Box 6 is split: the upper half (labeled OLB) shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow, and the lower half shows a solid up arrow. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow. A caption under the key reads OLA and OLB include slot clearance.

Title block caption: Left jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines, Slot Clearance. Sheet 11 of 12, drawing S-100.0.
notes:
Install where:
a) 40' <= D <= 200', and
b) there have been 4 or more right angle accidents or 4 or more left turn accidents in a recent 12 month period at one of the intersections involving vehicles departing from the interior limit line.
OLA and OLB include slot clearance.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections: Left Jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines, Slot Clearance (Sheet 11 of 12)
summary: Sheet 11 of 12 shows a left jogged intersection with interior limit lines and slot clearance overlaps OLA and OLB. It applies where D is from 40 ft to 200 ft and there have been 4 or more right angle or 4 or more left turn accidents in a recent 12 month period involving vehicles departing from the interior limit line. Programmed visibility cut-off heads show green and red only.

description:
Plan view, Right jogged intersection, interior limit lines: the arterial runs vertically. The minor street enters in two offset legs, the left leg at the upper left and the right leg at the lower right, separated along the arterial by a gap. Interior limit lines are drawn as rows of small circles across the arterial at the top and the bottom of the intersection box, labeled PV (G,R only), with callouts OLA PV CUT-OFF at the top and OLB PV CUT-OFF at the bottom. Overlap labels OLA and OLB appear on arrows and heads. Dimension D is drawn on the left between the interior limit lines. Back-to-back left-turn lanes are shown with an S-curved painted median and left-turn arrows at the top and in the gap. Mastarm poles carry heads and arrows for phases 2, 4, 6 and 8, with R9-3a signs (shown as R9-3a'S) at the inner corners. Pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P with APS pushbuttons sit at the corners.

Phase key: a 2 by 4 grid. Boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 2 is split by a dashed horizontal line: the upper half shows a dashed two-headed arrow beside a solid down arrow, and the lower half (labeled OLA) shows a solid down arrow. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid left arrow. Box 6 is split: the upper half (labeled OLB) shows a solid up arrow, and the lower half shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow. A caption under the key reads OLA and OLB include slot clearance.

Title block caption: Right jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines. Sheet 12 of 12, drawing S-100.0.
notes:
1. Install where 40' <= D <= 200'.
2. Mask only the green and red lenses of the programmed visibility (PV) heads.
3. The back-to-back left-turn lanes, as shown, are possible only where D >= 70'. Where not possible, a left-turn lane in one direction, possibly with a left-turn restriction in the other direction, should be considered.
OLA and OLB include slot clearance.
title: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections: Right Jogged Intersection, Interior Limit Lines (Sheet 12 of 12)
summary: Sheet 12 of 12 shows a right jogged intersection with interior limit lines and slot clearance overlaps OLA and OLB, for D from 40 ft to 200 ft. Only the green and red lenses of the programmed visibility heads are masked. Back-to-back left-turn lanes between the legs need D of 70 ft or more.

description:
Plan view, T intersection: the arterial runs vertically with a double centerline and left-turn arrows near the bottom. One minor street leg enters from the left. Left-turn pocket lane lines run on the arterial with a curved median nose near the top. Mastarm poles at the left corners carry heads for phase 2 (arrow up) and phase 6, with APS pushbuttons labeled phi 4 APS and phi 8 APS. Pedestrian heads 2P, 4P and 8P are shown at the left corners. On the east side of the arterial, a pole with a pedestrian head 4P and 8P, phase 4 APS and phase 8 APS pushbuttons carries heads for phases 6 and 8 and a phase 2 arrow. A highmount signal head with a phase 8 arrow is labeled Highmount.

Phase key: a 2 by 4 grid with boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 crossed out. Box 2 shows a dashed two-headed vertical arrow with a solid down arrow. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow.

Title block: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts, sheet 1 of 8, drawing S-101.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. Drawn by EC, dated 6-10-10. Approved June 24, 2010, signed for Rita L. Robinson, General Manager.
notes:
Highmount: if approach is one lane, then this head should be deleted.
This drawing is not intended to show the required safety lighting design. Final lighting designs may not include the depicted mastarm lighting and likely will include other lighting locations not shown.
title: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts: T Intersection (Sheet 1 of 8)
summary: Sheet 1 of 8 of drawing S-101.0 shows the typical signal head, pedestrian head and mastarm layout for a T intersection. A highmount head on the east side is deleted if the approach is one lane. The sheet was approved June 24, 2010.

description:
Plan view, 4-leg intersection: the arterial runs vertically with a double centerline, a left-turn arrow at the bottom and a left-turn lane arrow at the top. The minor street crosses it horizontally with two lanes in each direction approach. Four corner poles carry the signal heads. The upper-left pole has phase 4 APS and a 2P pedestrian head and a 4P pedestrian head, with a phase 6 arrow and a phase 4 arrow. The lower-left pole has phase 8 APS, 8P and 2P pedestrian heads, a mastarm over the arterial with a phase 2 arrow and phase 2 heads, and a phase 4 arrow. The upper-right pole has phase 4 APS, 6P and 4P pedestrian heads, a mastarm over the arterial with a phase 6 head and phase 6 and phase 8 arrows. The lower-right pole has phase 8 APS, 6P and 8P pedestrian heads and phase 2 and phase 8 arrows. Corner curb returns are drawn at all four corners with crosswalk lines on all four legs.

Phase key: a 2 by 4 grid with boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 crossed out. Box 2 shows a dashed two-headed vertical arrow beside a solid down arrow. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid left arrow. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow.

title: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts: 4-Leg Intersection (Sheet 2 of 8)
summary: Sheet 2 of 8 of drawing S-101.0 shows the typical signal head, pedestrian head and mastarm layout for a 4-leg intersection with the arterial running vertically and the minor street horizontally. The only note is that the sheet does not show the required safety lighting design.

description:
Plan view, one-way street: a one-way arterial runs vertically with traffic traveling up, shown by a large outline arrow in the lanes. A two-way minor street crosses it horizontally. A dimension line across the arterial lanes at the top has a leader to the text Not less than 20' and Not greater than 35', giving the mastarm length from the corner pole to the signal head over the lanes. Mastarm poles at the upper left and upper right corners carry phase 6 heads over the arterial lanes, with phase 4 APS pushbuttons, pedestrian heads 2P, 4P and 6P, and phase 4 and phase 8 arrows on the minor street. The lower corners carry phase 8 APS pushbuttons with pedestrian heads 2P, 6P and 8P and the phase 2 and phase 8 arrows. Minor street heads include phase 4 and phase 8 arrows on short mastarms into the minor street lanes.

Phase key: a 2 by 4 grid with boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 crossed out. Box 2 shows a dashed two-headed vertical arrow only. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid left arrow. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow.

Title block: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts, sheet 3 of 8, drawing S-101.0.
notes:
Notes:
1. For one-way streets with a roadway width less than 46 feet, a single mastarm signal head with the mastarm signal head placed within 5 feet of the center of the approach lane(s) should be installed.
2. This drawing is not intended to show the required safety lighting design. Final lighting designs may not include the depicted mastarm lighting and likely will include other lighting locations not shown.
Dimension callout: Not less than 20' and not greater than 35'.
title: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts: One Way Street (Sheet 3 of 8)
summary: Sheet 3 of 8 of drawing S-101.0 shows the typical signal head layout for a one-way arterial. The mastarm length shown is not less than 20 ft and not greater than 35 ft. For roadways under 46 feet wide, a single mastarm head within 5 feet of the center of the approach lanes is used.

description:
Plan view, left-turn phasing: the arterial runs vertically with a double centerline and left-turn arrows near the top and bottom. The minor street crosses it horizontally with a left-turn arrow on each side. Near-side primary heads using triple-arrow indications for phase 1 are drawn at the upper left corner and on the mastarm over the arterial at the top. A callout near the lower right corner reads: For each approach having protected left-turn phasing, a near side primary signal head is added. This is not necessary for protected permissive phasing. Corner poles carry heads and arrows for phases 2, 4, 6 and 8, with phase 2 APS, 4 APS, 6 APS and 8 APS pushbuttons and pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P at the corners.

Phase key: a 2 by 4 grid. Boxes 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 1 shows a curved arrow turning left (the protected left turn). Box 2 shows a dashed two-headed vertical arrow beside a solid down arrow. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid left arrow. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow.

Title block: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts, sheet 4 of 8, drawing S-101.0.
notes:
For each approach having protected left-turn phasing, a near side primary signal head is added. This is not necessary for protected permissive phasing. (Callout on the plan.)
Notes:
1. Protected left-turn phasing is shown. See S-65.0 for mastarm head placement for other types of left-turn phasing.
2. This drawing is not intended to show the required safety lighting design. Final lighting designs may not include the depicted mastarm lighting and likely will include other lighting locations not shown.
title: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts: Left-Turn Phasing (Sheet 4 of 8)
summary: Sheet 4 of 8 of drawing S-101.0 shows the typical signal head layout where the arterial has protected left-turn phasing (phase 1). A near side primary signal head is added for each approach with protected left-turn phasing, which is not needed for protected permissive phasing.

description:
Plan view, signalized driveway: the arterial runs vertically with a double centerline and left-turn arrows in the upper and lower portions. On the left, a two-lane minor street joins it. On the right, a driveway runs along the right edge and is drawn with a box crossed out for the driveway opening and a label Driveway. Corner poles carry heads and arrows for phases 2, 4, 6 and 8 with phase 4 APS and phase 8 APS pushbuttons and pedestrian heads 2P, 4P, 6P and 8P. Two phase 4 heads on the left minor street leg are tagged R/FL.R. with callouts that read See Detail "A" and Note 3. A text block beside the plan reads: Where phase 8 traffic is moderately high or where the driveway is offset from the side street then opposed phasing should be considered.

Detail A, phase 4: a three-section vertical signal head with, from top to bottom, R (red), FL.R. (flashing red) and Y (yellow).
Detail B, phase 4: a three-section vertical signal head with, from top to bottom, R (red), Y (yellow) and FL.Y. (flashing yellow).

Phase key: a 2 by 4 grid with boxes 1, 3, 5 and 7 crossed out. Box 2 shows a dashed two-headed vertical arrow beside a solid down arrow. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid left arrow labeled R/FL.R. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow with a dashed two-headed arrow beside it. Box 8 shows a solid right arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow.

Title block: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts, sheet 5 of 8, drawing S-101.0.
notes:
Where phase 8 traffic is moderately high or where the driveway is offset from the side street then opposed phasing should be considered. (Text on the plan.)
Notes:
1. This typical design is appropriate where a review of use has determined that the driveway should be signalized. Normally, this design would be used only where the driveway could not easily be reconstructed to be configured with curb returns and a "step down" design along the path of pedestrians. New development driveways with higher traffic volumes at intersections should be required to construct street like driveways with a layout for a "T" or 4-leg intersection, as appropriate.
2. This drawing is not intended to show the required safety lighting design. Final lighting designs may not include the depicted mastarm lighting and likely will include other lighting locations not shown.
3. Detail "B" may be used where visibility is good and a flashing yellow indication provides adequate control of driveway traffic.
Legend: R = red, FL.R. = flashing red, Y = yellow, FL.Y. = flashing yellow.
title: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts: Signalized Driveway (Sheet 5 of 8)
summary: Sheet 5 of 8 of drawing S-101.0 shows a signalized driveway typical on a minor street with the driveway as the east leg. Detail A uses a red, flashing red and yellow head and Detail B a red, yellow and flashing yellow head for the phase 4 driveway approach. Notes limit the design to cases where the driveway cannot be rebuilt with curb returns and a step-down design.

description:
Plan view, signalized midblock crosswalk, two way street: a two-way street runs vertically with a double centerline and a left-turn style median taper. A 20' wide ladder crosswalk crosses it, with a dimension X between the crosswalk and the upper edge of the set-back zone and a 5' min. dimension at the top and bottom. An overall dimension of 50' min. spans from the mastarm poles on one side of the crosswalk to the other. Mastarm poles at the upper right and lower left carry vehicle heads for phases 6 and 2, pointing at Details A and B. Pedestrian heads 4P and phase 4 APS pushbuttons sit at both ends of the crosswalk, with phase 6 and phase 2 arrows.

Detail A: a PED XING sign hung from a mastarm, black letters on yellow background.
Detail B: a three-section vertical signal head labeled from top to bottom FL.R, Y and G, with the bottom lens a green up arrow.
Detail C: a plan of the approach where X > 10' (See Note 3): the pedestrian head 4P is on a pole at the crosswalk, and a separate pole at the limit line carries the phase 6 secondary vehicle head. The legend WAIT HERE is painted in the approach lanes (inverted in the plan) in front of the limit line, with a 10' dimension X between the limit line and the crosswalk.

Phase key: a 2 by 4 grid with boxes 1, 3, 5, 7 and 8 crossed out. Box 2 shows a solid down arrow. Box 4 shows a dashed two-headed arrow. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow.

Title block: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts, sheet 6 of 8, drawing S-101.0.
notes:
Notes:
1. Signal equipment should be combined with street lighting where feasible.
2. See S-493.0, Cases 13 & 14 for limit line locations. See S-481.0 for ladder crosswalk detail.
3. Where X is greater than 10', install a pole for the pedestrian head at the location shown, and a separate pole for the secondary vehicle head at the limit line, as shown in Detail "C".
4. This drawing is not intended to show the required safety lighting design. Final lighting designs may not include the depicted mastarm lighting and likely will include other lighting locations not shown.
5. During Phase 4 pedestrian sequence, Phases 2 & 6 receive a flashing red signal display.
Detail labels: Detail "A": black letters on yellow background. Dimension labels: X > 10', see Note 3; 5' min.; 20'; 50' min.
title: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts: Signalized Midblock Crosswalk, Two Way Street (Sheet 6 of 8)
summary: Sheet 6 of 8 of drawing S-101.0 shows a signalized midblock crosswalk on a two-way street with mastarms, pedestrian heads, a PED XING sign and a flashing red display for phases 2 and 6 during the phase 4 pedestrian sequence. Where X is more than 10 ft, separate poles are used for the pedestrian head and the secondary vehicle head (Detail C).

description:
Plan view, signalized midblock crosswalk, one way street: a one-way street runs vertically with a large outline arrow showing the direction up and dashed lane lines. A ladder crosswalk 20' wide crosses it. Dimensions of 50' min. and 5' min. are shown on the left, and a 20' dimension for the crosswalk width. Mastarm poles at each curb carry phase 2 heads over the lanes, tagged Detail "B", and a PED XING sign (Detail "A") hangs on the mastarms. A dimension across the lanes between the two mastarm heads has the callout Not less than 20' and Not greater than 35'. Pedestrian heads 4P with phase 4 APS pushbuttons sit at each end of the crosswalk, and phase 2 arrows point at the approach.

Detail B: a three-section vertical signal head, labeled from top to bottom FL.R, Y and G, with the bottom lens a green up arrow.

notes:
Notes:

title: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts: Signalized Midblock Crosswalk, One Way Street (Sheet 7 of 8)
summary: Sheet 7 of 8 of drawing S-101.0 shows a signalized midblock crosswalk on a one-way street. Mastarm poles on both curbs are 50 ft min. from the crosswalk, with a mastarm length of not less than 20 ft and not greater than 35 ft, and phase 2 receives a flashing red during the phase 4 pedestrian sequence.

description:
Plan view, intersection with signalized frontage road: an arterial runs vertically with a double centerline on the left and a frontage road runs on the right, separated by a median. A cross street enters from the left. A 20' (shown as a bold less-than sign and 20') dimension is drawn at the bottom of the frontage road leg and a 50' min. dimension at the top across the width of the frontage road median opening. The words KEEP CLEAR are painted twice (inverted in the plan) between the arterial and frontage road. A vertical row of dots along the frontage road edge is labeled PV Cutoff OLA. Left side: mastarm heads for phases 2, 4, 6 and 8 with PV OLA (G,R only) heads, each tagged High mount at 14'. Median pole clusters carry R13A, R9-3A(2) and R9-3B(2) signs and a TOP MOUNT head, with phase 8 APS and phase 4 APS pushbuttons, pedestrian heads 2P, 4P and 8P and phase 1 and phase 4 arrows. Right side: corner poles with phase 4 APS, pedestrian heads 1P and 4P and R13A and R10-6 signs with phase 1 arrows.

Phase key: a 2 by 4 grid split by a dashed vertical line into main street phases on the left and frontage road phases on the right. Box 1 (outlined in bold, labeled EXCLUSIVE) shows OLA with a left arrow, a solid down arrow, and a dashed up arrow with down arrowhead. Box 2 shows a dashed two-headed vertical arrow beside a solid down arrow. Boxes 3, 5 and 7 are crossed out. Box 4 (labeled OLA) shows a solid left arrow above a dashed two-headed arrow, with a dashed two-headed arrow in the frontage portion. Box 6 shows a solid up arrow. Box 8 shows a dashed two-headed arrow above a solid right arrow and another dashed two-headed arrow. A caption under the key reads OLA Includes Slot Clearance.

Title block: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts, sheet 8 of 8, drawing S-101.0.
notes:
NOTES:
1. This drawing is not intended to show the required safety lighting design. Final lighting designs may not include the depicted mastarm lighting and likely will include other lighting locations not shown.
2. Mask only the green and red lenses of the programmed visibility (PV) heads.
3. To be used in Case 9 of S-493.0.
Plan labels: EXCLUSIVE, OLA Includes Slot Clearance, PV Cutoff OLA, TOP MOUNT, High mount at 14', 50' min., R13A, R9-3A(2), R9-3B(2), R10-6.
title: Typical Traffic Signal Layouts: Intersection with Signalized Frontage Road (Sheet 8 of 8)
summary: Sheet 8 of 8 of drawing S-101.0 shows a typical signal layout for an intersection with a signalized frontage road, with programmed visibility heads, high mount heads at 14 ft and signs R13A, R9-3A(2), R9-3B(2) and R10-6. It is to be used in Case 9 of S-493.0, and overlap OLA includes slot clearance.
